# Welcome {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| include: false
# This chunk activates knitr for inline code
```

This online resource shares materials from the "Integrating Generative AI into R Workflows: From APIs to Shiny Apps" workshop, first presented at the inaugural AIMECON meeting in October, 2025, and later at NCME Annual Meeting in Los Angeles in April 2026. 
The current iteration of the workshop is for [AIMECON](https://ncme.org/events/aime-conference/) again, where it will be presented on Monday, October 5th from 1pm-5pm EST.

The workshop assumes some working knowledge of the R programming language, and assumes little generative AI knowledge. If you need more information on using R, I highly recommend Hadley Wickham's (free) [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/).

## How to Use This Site

Begin with [Setup](01-R-setup.qmd) to prepare R and your API access. The next sections introduce generative AI and its parameters before moving into practical R workflows, including conversations, batch processing, and chained prompts. The final section uses Shiny and AI-assisted coding to build interactive applications.

Read in order for the workshop experience, or use the sidebar to return to a specific topic. Activities and downloadable notebooks are included throughout; some examples call external model APIs and may use your account's credits.

<div style="font-size: 1.75em; font-weight: bold; margin-top: 1em; color: black;">
Learning Objectives
</div>

[By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to:]{.underline}

-	Explain key LLM architectural features that inform effective integration practices
-	Implement both conversational and transactional API interactions with LLMs from R
-	Design and deploy simple chained prompt workflows for complex tasks
-	Build interactive Shiny applications that leverage LLM capabilities for end-user functionality
